_comment: verify-gate-enforcement manifest — closes catalog class G1 (gate-enforcement vacuity) from docs/verification/fv-adversarial-review-playbook.md Part A2. Each soundness/anti-vacuity gate declares WHAT source surface it polices, WHICH workflow must run it, and its ENFORCEMENT level. check_gate_enforcement.py asserts the live CI wiring matches — a gate that is green-when-run but never RUNS on the diff it polices (wrong `paths:` filter, `continue-on-error`, workflow_dispatch-only, `|| true` on the invocation line, a statically-false `if:`, a comment-only invocation, or unwired) is exactly as dangerous as a hollow proof (the 2026-07-01 F1 finding: verify-ledger-consistency never fired on AXIOM_STATUS.json-only edits; the 2026-08-20 #663 neutralization classes). enforcement: 'per_pr_blocking' = must run on push/pull_request, non-continue-on-error, and the trigger `paths:` must COVER polices_paths; 'nightly' = must be invoked by a scheduled workflow (blocking checks apply to this tier too); 'local_documented' = deliberately not CI-gated (a NOTE, never a failure) — must carry a `why` with a DATED ISSUE REFERENCE (#NNN or YYYY-MM-DD), and any declared `runs_in` must name a workflow that actually invokes the target. polices_paths are repo-relative prefixes/globs the gate is responsible for. Blocking gates pin the complete parsed invocation step and runner context. The independent ENFORCEMENT_POLICY in the checker pins every registered identity and level; editing this manifest alone cannot remove/demote a gate. All policy/context updates require source review. No arbitrary shell-execution or hosted-settings proof is claimed.

Zero-width (U+200B..U+200F/U+FEFF) and bidi override/isolate (U+202A..U+202E, U+2066..U+2069) codepoints are invisible to git diff and to code review. Two attacks share that mechanism: TrapDoor-style poisoning of the AI-instruction files every coding agent executes, and Trojan Source (CVE-2021-42574). Baseline 2026-07-31 is ZERO hits over 3841 tracked text files with NO allowlist — the two pre-existing hits were fixed, not exempted, because an allowlist here is a place to hide the payload. Carries a two-sided self-test (5 payload classes fire, 3 benign inputs stay silent); ordinary non-ASCII is deliberately allowed or the gate would be red on day one and disabled by the end of the week.

gates.why: The three 100-byte-symbolic multiSend harnesses (per_record_page_bound 12.71 GiB/6m03s, no_hidden_value 13.05 GiB/7m55s, cow_presign_precedence 11.50 GiB/3m56s; all VERIFY SUCCESSFULLY, measured locally 2026-07-31) exceed what a hosted runner can absorb. Instrumented CI evidence 2026-07-31: the runner has 15,989 MB RAM with 14,497 MB available and 145 GB disk with 86 GB free, so DISK IS NOT THE CAUSE - it is memory. The kill lands between 'Runtime Postprocess Equation' and 'Solving with ...', i.e. inside CBMC's formula construction and BEFORE any SAT solver is invoked; a kissat experiment was therefore reverted, since the solver never runs. (That experiment's local peak-RSS numbers were also unsound: an external solver runs out-of-process and /usr/bin/time -v reports a per-process maximum, not an aggregate.) Excluded because an OOM kills the runner and suppresses every later mandatory gate in the same job - same reasoning as verify-extracted-heavy (53c19f21); continue-on-error cannot save a dead runner. The 100-byte bound is deliberately NOT reduced: shrinking a proof's bound to earn a green check is coverage loss disguised as a pass. Larger hosted runners are unavailable (Team/Enterprise-only; this org is free-plan; hosted-runners API 404s). Run via `make kani-heavy`; the other 170 harnesses stay blocking in nightly. runs_in=nightly.yml dropped 2026-08-20 (#664) — no workflow invokes the target.

step.name: Read-only Ethereum observation
step.run:
make erc7730-proxy-drift
python3 - <<'PY'
import json
import os
from pathlib import Path

report = json.loads(Path("target/erc7730-proxy-drift.json").read_text())
summary = report["summary"]
rows = [
    "## ERC-7730 proxy drift (advisory only)",
    "",
    f"MATCH: {summary['MATCH']} · DRIFT: {summary['DRIFT']} · UNKNOWN: {summary['UNKNOWN']}",
    "",
    "This observation grants no signing, catalogue, release, or production authority.",
]
with open(os.environ["GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"], "a", encoding="utf-8") as output:
    output.write("\n".join(rows) + "\n")
if summary["DRIFT"]:
    print(f"::warning::{summary['DRIFT']} watched ERC-7730 proxy row(s) drifted")
if summary["UNKNOWN"]:
    print(f"::warning::{summary['UNKNOWN']} watched ERC-7730 proxy row(s) are unknown")
PY
